netlist:
C Cin VIN1 n1
L Lg n1 n2
NMOS M1 n4 n2 n3 VSS
L Ls n3 VSS
L Ld VDD n4
C Ct1 n4 n5
C Ct2 n5 VSS
C Cout n5 VOUT1
rationale: The chosen topology is an inductively degenerated common-source LNA with a tapped-capacitor output load, leveraging the 45nm bulk CMOS process's ability to integrate compact inductors while achieving excellent input matching and low noise. The inductive degeneration (Lg) at the gate provides a low-impedance path to ground at 3.5 GHz, enhancing input match (S11) and improving noise figure by reducing gate resistance. The tapped capacitor (Ct1/Ct2) enables a high-Q resonant output load, achieving high gain (S21) with minimal current consumption. The use of a single NMOS transistor minimizes device count, respecting the device budget, while the inductor in the source (Ls) further improves stability and noise performance through impedance transformation. This topology is well-suited for the 3.5 GHz target, where input match is critical (S11 ≤ -11 dB), and NF ≤ 2.8 dB is achievable with careful tuning.
